question: Can bounded causal admission preserve an already playing accepted critical consequence during later lower-priority observations without inventing game outcomes or growing beyond two voices?
baseline: The existing two-voice FIFO adapter protects terminal arrival by clearing voices, but later accepted begin/contact/threat cues can stop the still-playing 0.60-second terminal cue.
intervention: Keep the existing ten original Composer WAVs, actual accepted C# game observations and aligned stems; use C# priority descriptors and finite admission decisions in the existing browser adapter.

hypotheses.prediction: The actual survey win followed immediately by accepted second begin and action preserves terminal ownership and its later effects-only PCM tail while never exceeding two active voices.
An incoming lower-priority threat cannot stop a playing contact; equal-contact saturation explicitly suppresses new content instead of silently claiming complete delivery.

rivals_and_controls: A changed gameplay result could explain the apparent improvement: retain the actual accepted snapshots, action order and sequence identities.
A longer or louder replacement terminal recording could explain tail energy: require exact preservation of all ten original Composer WAV identities.
History could claim a surviving voice after audio was cut: capture final AudioContext PCM continuously while actual commands execute and check a terminal-only late window.

Music or a later effect could explain terminal tail energy: set music to zero and bound the late interval after every later admitted short effect has ended but before the original terminal buffer ends.

An ineffective instrument could accept broken playback: serve an isolated mutation of the actual current adapter that cuts critical audio and require the same terminal criterion to fail with successful game commands.
A muted, stale or resumed observation could bypass the budget: test actual mute/suspend/resume, repeated GET/observation and interrupted asynchronous decode.
A silent capture could falsely pass headroom: require nonzero nominal PCM and reject an actual excess-master-gain fixture.
A phase-only claim could miss source misalignment: require real shared-harmonic capture and detect an isolated 37 ms delay on one captured stem path.
acceptance: Actual terminal observation plus at least two accepted later commands overlap within the terminal duration; the critical voice is neither stopped nor suppressed by a lower-priority event.
Actual effects-only terminal tail has more than 512 observed frames and RMS greater than 0.001 after later admitted effects end, with nominal output peak below 0.9.
At most two active voices exist in every inspected snapshot; same-priority critical overflow has explicit suppression evidence and does not replay later.
The same capture criterion detects an actual isolated critical-cut policy mutation; process, browser, command or environment errors cannot count as a detected negative.
Mute produces measured final-output silence and consumes sequence; suspension actually stops the context and voices; explicit resume has no prior-event backlog.
Source and producer hashes remain stable across the final execution, with complete command/environment logs and raw captures outside maintained sources.
not_measured: ITU-R BS.1770 true peak or LUFS
Perceived recognition, masking, preference, realism or comfort
Hardware playback, listener studies or ordinary-user devices
Unity Editor, Windows Player or Steam execution
Commercial rights or redistribution permission for the 48 archive media assets

source_basis.intake: P08 V6 offline counterexamples and causal consumer boundary; archive kept outside the maintained tree
source_basis.material_influence: Competing explanations require unchanged game/source identities, actual output, a policy negative and separate signal/perception conclusions.
